subject: Re: Alphacorp - sudden latency regression and errors
messages:
From: Jessica Nguyen <jessica.nguyen@alphacorp.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai
Cc: sam.richards@alphacorp.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Latency spike impacting checkout - urgent

Hi Vivek / Redwood support,

We started seeing a sharp regression in response times to your hosted API around 02:10 UTC today. Our metrics show p95 climbed from ~400ms to ~3.2s and p99 into the 6-8s range for the /v1/generate route. We're also seeing ~2% 500 errors that correlate with higher tail latency. This began right after your platform deployment window yesterday (we were notified of a minor runtime patch).

Impact: it’s causing intermittent failures in checkout workflows for ~8% of sessions (AlphaCorp US customers). We have attached a small trace bundle and sample request IDs. Please advise immediate mitigations and what the root cause is.

Attachments: alphacorp_latency_trace_20260114.zip (log bundle, 12MB)

Thanks,
Jessica Nguyen
Senior SRE, AlphaCorp
jessica.nguyen@alphacorp.com

Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting checkout - urgent

Jessica —

Thanks for the signal and the trace bundle. We're treating this as P1 and I’ve looped in engineering (Laura + Marcus) and Customer Success (Monica). Initial ask: can you share 3-5 request IDs with the highest p99 from the bundle so we can correlate to our request logs? I’ll get an incident channel going and update here within 30 minutes.

We understand the user impact; apologies for the disruption.

—Vivek

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: jessica.nguyen@alphacorp.com, sam.richards@alphacorp.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting checkout - urgent

Quick technical update after a short triage:

What we saw
- Around 02:08 UTC a config rollout changed the in-memory prefix eviction threshold on a small subset of serving pools (commit bb9f3a2).
- That change caused a coordinated eviction of cached KV prefixes for sessions with shared prefixes (hot prefixes).
- When cache entries were evicted, requests hit cold KV paths that trigger synchronous disk lookups + KV-decode path, causing per-request latency to balloon. Because many sessions share prefixes in AlphaCorp workload, there was a brief "warm-up storm" where p95/p99 spiked.
- Error rate (~2%) aligns with request timeouts at the RPC layer when backend retries hit the time budget.

Immediate actions taken (in last 60m)
- Rolled back the eviction threshold change on the affected pools (rollback applied at 10:42 UTC).
- Enabled temporary extra capacity (burst nodes) for AlphaCorp routing.
- Kicked off a targeted KV pre-warm for the top 500 prefixes observed in your traces.

Proposed mitigation plan
1) Patch: revert the threshold change in prod permanently and add a staged rollout with throttled invalidations. ETA: 24 hours.
2) Short-term: keep burst capacity and continue prefix pre-warm for 24–48 hours.
3) Medium-term: introduce a conservative hot-prefix pinning feature (configurable per-customer) and increase default prefix TTL for high-hotkey workloads. ETA: 3 weeks for rollout + QA.
4) Compensate affected customers if SLOs were breached during the incident window — recommend a credit and a follow-up RCA call.

Attachments: kv_eviction_summary_20260114.pdf, dgraph_kv_eviction.png

Laura Bennett
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: jessica.nguyen@alphacorp.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 12:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting checkout - urgent

Additional technical notes + quick mitigation steps we executed:

- Observed KV miss rate for top-1k prefixes rose from <1% to ~42% between 02:05–02:20 UTC.
- Root cause: the eviction policy update reduced per-shard in-memory residency and triggered vectorized eviction during compaction.

Hot fixes applied:
- Route AlphaCorp traffic to a warmed replica fleet for 2 hours (reduced p99 by ~60%).
- Applied a targeted prefix pre-warm job (k8s job) which filled the top hot prefixes into memory; job completed in ~45m.
- Temporarily increased request timeout thresholds for the checkout route to reduce user-facing 500s while warm-up continues.

Risk & next steps:
- The rollback is stable but we need to harden rollout processes to prevent similar global invalidations.
- ETA for the conservative hot-prefix pinning feature is ~3 weeks but we can backport a simpler per-customer TTL override within 5 business days.

Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Jessica Nguyen <jessica.nguyen@alphacorp.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: sam.richards@alphacorp.com, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting checkout - urgent

Thanks for the fast response and the mitigation steps — we can confirm tail has come down after your warm replica routing but we still saw a p99 blip this morning during a traffic surge (around 07:12 UTC). We appreciate the pre-warm job.

Two asks from AlphaCorp:
1) Can Redwood commit to a concrete timeline for the per-customer TTL override (5 business days is acceptable if you can meet it).
2) Please outline proposed SLA credit for the impacted window (we measured ~45 minutes where checkout failures exceeded our accepted threshold).

We’d like an exec-level point of contact for the credit conversation. Also, please keep us posted about the permanent rollout changes.

Jessica

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: jessica.nguyen@alphacorp.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Alphacorp escalation — exec summary and next steps

Team — short exec summary to coordinate customer-facing asks and approvals:

Summary of event:
- Incident window (rough): 2026-01-14 02:05–02:50 UTC. Cause: rollout-induced KV/prefix eviction leading to cache warm-up storm and p95/p99 regressions.
- Impact: AlphaCorp saw checkout p99 spikes (6–8s) and ~2% 500s for ~45 minutes; mitigations reduced tail ~60% and full stability restored after targeted warm-up and rollback.

Customer asks:
- Per-customer TTL override delivered within 5 business days.
- SLA credit for the 45-minute window (AlphaCorp will propose amount; recommend we offer credit proactively).
- Exec-level POC for credit and contract discussion: I will be primary, Monica to coordinate CS details.

Proposed internal asks for approvals:
1) Approve a goodwill credit for AlphaCorp (suggest 10% of January invoice pro-rated for incident duration) — Monica please advise if there is an existing guideline we should follow.
2) Approve priority engineering slot to implement the per-customer TTL override within 5 business days (requires two engineers for 3 days + QA).
3) Approve commitment to a formal RCA (doc + postmortem) and an external call with AlphaCorp leadership next week.

I’m looping Marissa to escalate to Commercial leadership if we need exceptions on credit or contract terms.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
